review.brief:
Review the RM28 tier-4 gateway change across commits 7831f0e, 7c2e1ec, 13d3dc9 (read the DIFF, not the whole module). Validate:
1. MODULE BOUNDARY. internal/gateway touches internal/battery ONLY through battery.Reader / battery.DayConsumption. No database access, no other module's internals. cmd/web (T7) was the leader's, outside the module sandbox.
2. DOC-PACK CONVENTIONS. ai/go-conventions.md, ai/architecture.md, ai/htmx-conventions.md, ai/htmx-go-integration.md, internal/gateway/AGENTS.md. Specifically: no HTML outside the gateway; no arithmetic or domain-method calls in the template (RD7); display units unchanged.
3. i18n. Every new user-facing string resolves through i18n.T with BOTH ES and EN non-empty. Seven new keys. D-G7 makes three of them composable CLAUSES joined by ' · ' — confirm the composition cannot produce a dangling separator or an untranslated fragment in either language.
4. OWNER DECISIONS, verbatim. D10 (flagged day: zero height, number hidden), D11 (default AND cap move to yesterday), D18 (bucket in Config.Location — the gateway must key on DayConsumption.Date VERBATIM and must NOT re-project through effectiveDayUTC; D-G2 is the regression guard), D19 (relative scale, mirroring buildOdometerChart), D20 (multi-day span plots its REAL value), D21 (a day both flagged and spanned carries BOTH markers with both facts in the tooltip — markers are a set, not an enum).
5. TEST CONTRACT (Step 3's rule). design.md's Test Contract was authored BEFORE implementation. Verify T8's tests assert THOSE expectations, not whatever buildConsumedChart happens to do. Any test that merely restates the implementation is a finding.
6. TWO ITEMS THE LEADER IS DELIBERATELY SURFACING RATHER THAN BURYING:
   (a) The worker added Consumed: HistoryChart{Empty:true} to the two DashboardHistoryFragment early returns (400, no-vehicle). NOT in design.md or tasks.md; leader accepted it (D4) because both literals already set Odometer and Battery that way. Confirm or reject that reading.
   (b) newHandlerForHistory never set Deps.BatteryReader while buildHistoryView calls ConsumedByDay unconditionally — a nil-interface panic latent from wave 2, invisible to build and vet because vet compiles tests without running them. Fixed in wave 3. ASK WHETHER ANYTHING ELSE IN THIS TIER SHIPPED PAST A SIGNAL THAT STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT SEE IT.
7. A SPECIFIC CORRECTNESS QUESTION THE LEADER WANTS CHECKED. buildConsumedChart keys a map[time.Time] on DayConsumption.Date and looks it up with the loop variable derived from `start`. time.Time map keys compare wall clock AND location. Confirm both sides are genuinely UTC midnight in practice (battery's calendarDay normalization vs parseHistoryRange's start, which carries a browser timezone in the D11 path) — a silent mismatch would make every bucket lookup miss and render an all-no-data chart with no error anywhere.
8. ANTI-GAMING. Tasks/criteria are append-only. T8.15 and T8.16 were APPENDED by the leader (D7); verify nothing existing was edited, weakened, or deleted. V.3 is deliberately unchecked (D6) — five pre-existing gofmt-dirty files outside this tier, not swept.
TEST-EXECUTION-POLICY (verbatim): Claude writes tests but never runs the suite — never go test ./..., make test, make test-with-db or make check. It MAY run go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make build, make vet, make bins, and the standalone guards make ui-guard / make i18n-guard / make money-guard. The owner runs the suite and reports results.
WHICH SIGNALS WERE WHOSE: assistant-run — go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make ui-guard, make i18n-guard, the app.css fill-* grep, openspec validate --strict. USER-REPORTED — `make test` green against the complete tier (2026-08-16). Judge test QUALITY by READING the tests; do not run them.

findings.note: buildConsumedChart's byDay map (history.go) is keyed on battery.DayConsumption.Date (always time.UTC, via internal/battery's calendarDay). The loop variable `d` used to read it derives from `start`, which is genuinely UTC only on the explicit-?start=&end= path (time.Parse defaults to UTC) and on the no-cookie fallback. On the D11 both-absent-params default path WITH a valid non-UTC browser_tz cookie, start/end/d carry that zone's *time.Location (browserToday->startOfDayIn), which is a different absolute instant AND a different Location pointer than the UTC map keys -- Go's own docs warn == (hence map lookup) compares Location too. Every d would then miss byDay, silently rendering all-no-data with no error logged. Verified via source: internal/battery/consumed.go calendarDay()/effectiveDay() (UTC only), internal/gateway/handlers/tz.go startOfDayIn/browserToday (preserves the cookie's Location), history.go:125-164 parseHistoryRange, and history_test.go's own TestParseHistoryRange_DefaultUsesBrowserYesterday which asserts end.Location()=="America/Bogota" for exactly this path -- proving the non-UTC Location is intentional/reachable there. NOT introduced or worsened by this tier: buildOdometerChart/buildBatteryChart (pre-existing, out of this tier's scope) share the identical byDay[d] read-side gap -- their write side uses effectiveDayUTC but their read side does not normalize d either. Unreachable through the actual product UI (defaultHistoryHref and buildHistoryPresets always send explicit params, which are always UTC via time.Parse); reachable only via a bare GET /ui/dashboard/history with no query params from an authenticated browser that already holds a non-UTC browser_tz cookie. design.md's D-G3 explicitly forbids adding new gateway-side timezone handling to buildConsumedChart, so a local fix here would be scope creep; the right place is a shared fix/decision at parseHistoryRange or browserToday, covering all three charts. Recommend the leader open a follow-up backlog item (mirroring how D18/D18a's UTC-vs-zoned mismatch was recorded as a known, accepted limitation) rather than reworking this tier.

decisions.decision: Wave 1 batches T1/T2/T4/T5 into one serial worker rather than four parallel ones
decisions.why: Tasks are small and disjoint; one dispatch amortizes the doc-pack read, and parallel workers drain the same 5-hour bucket faster for no wall-clock gain here.

decisions.why: Both literals already set Odometer and Battery the same way; leaving Consumed at its zero value would render a 0-bar SVG instead of the empty state. Flagged to the reviewer.
